title: Wine Wimsey Review · Oct 25
subtitle: 13 feed (11 images + 2 TOBIs at #4 and #10) and 4 stories, for posting Sun Oct 25 · all 15 inbox items used, oldest first, quotes word for word (11 feed, 4 stories) · Characters: 9 The Hot Mess, 5 The Homebody, 1 couple (#6) · 2 new TOBIs under 130 characters · Caption mix: 4 short, 7 See More · Flags: #9 has the grumpy cat you asked for; #11 has the candy bowl; “Picture yourself without wine” (story 4) is wine as the subject; #7 keeps the stray closing quote mark from your typed quote (the bubble dropped it); #2 shows a stray opening quote mark in the bubble; #6 is a couple, not the usual character

posts.quote: Be careful following the masses. Sometimes the “M” is silent.
posts.caption: I once followed a crowd into a building because everyone looked so certain. It was a dentist's office. Nobody had an appointment. We all stood there. I have never felt more like part of something.
posts.first: My sister says I overthink the herd thing. Then she told me everyone at her gym was doing a juice cleanse, and she was on day two. I asked how she felt. She said hungry. I rest my case and my glass.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a skeptical woman holding a glass of red wine, standing in a crowd of faceless gray silhouettes all marching the same way. Text at the top reads: Be careful following the masses. Sometimes the “M” is silent.

posts.quote: To end up old and wise, you first have to be young and stupid.
posts.caption: I'm fairly wise now. It cost me a perm that fried like a tumbleweed, a boyfriend named Gary, and a summer I spent convinced that frosted blue eyeshadow was a personality. I got a good price for the education. Every mistake came with a lesson, and every lesson came with a story I can now tell from the armchair.
posts.first: I keep a photo of that blue eyeshadow phase in a drawer, for perspective. When I'm tempted to feel too wise, I take it out. It brings me right back down, and I always end up laughing. Then I put it away.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a content woman with pink curls sitting in a floral armchair with a glass of white wine on a side table. Text at the top reads: To end up old and wise, you first have to be young and stupid.

posts.quote: People complain about it getting dark early, like ending up on the couch under a blanket is some kind of punishment.
posts.caption: The sun goes down at 5:15 now and my whole body says thank you. Lamp on, blanket out, slippers on, feet up. The day doesn't have a say in it anymore. I used to feel guilty about being in by six. Now I think of it as getting a head start on the best part.
posts.first: I have three blankets within reach of this couch and I rotate them like a seasonal menu. Tonight it's the cream fuzzy one. Nobody has asked me to go anywhere, and I'm not offering.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a blissful woman with pink curls snuggled on a couch under a fuzzy blanket holding a glass of red wine, with a lit lamp and a dark evening window behind her. Text at the top reads: People complain about it getting dark early, like ending up on the couch under a blanket is some kind of punishment.

posts.quote: I don't need a gym. I have a laundry basket, a flight of stairs, and a deep sense of resentment.
posts.first: Three trips a day and I'm already out of breath by the second landing. The resentment, at least, has excellent stamina.

posts.quote: I keep trying to cancel my 3 a.m. wake-up subscription. Apparently “exhausted and cranky” isn’t an acceptable reason.
posts.caption: 3:00 on the dot again. I lay there and reviewed every embarrassing thing I've said since 1997. The brain really does run a quality program at that hour. Very thorough. Zero requests from me.
posts.first: Last night I made it to 4:10 before the review ended. A personal best. The tea went cold on the nightstand and I drank it anyway, because by then it felt earned.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a wide-eyed, frazzled woman sitting up in bed in the dark with a glowing bedside clock reading 3:00 and a cup of tea on the nightstand. Text at the top reads: I keep trying to cancel my 3 a.m. wake-up subscription. Apparently “exhausted and cranky” isn’t an acceptable reason.

posts.character: The Hot Mess and a husband
posts.quote: He says: “Women don’t look cute drinking wine.” She says: “I’m not drinking it to look cute. I’m drinking it so you look cute.”
posts.caption: Thirty years of marriage taught me that he is right about very little and wrong about the rest. He watched me pour a generous glass and said his piece, arms crossed, plaid shirt, full confidence. I took a sip. He got cuter right away. The wine is doing exactly what I hired it for, and it's very good at it.
posts.first: He's actually a sweetheart. He just says things at the wrong moment and then spends a day making up for it. Tonight he's making dinner. I'm in the kitchen supervising, and I'm told I'm looking cute.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a smug man in a plaid shirt with arms crossed beside a woman with a messy bun and glasses on her forehead holding a big glass of red wine with a deadpan smile, in a cozy kitchen. Text at the top reads: He says: “Women don’t look cute drinking wine.” She says: “I’m not drinking it to look cute. I’m drinking it so you look cute.”

posts.quote: Don’t you get bored being home all the time?” Meanwhile I bake, garden, read, rearrange my treasures, try new recipes, watch my shows, play music, sit outside, do little projects, and enjoy my own company. With zero nonsense.
posts.caption: Last week I rearranged one shelf and it took the whole afternoon. I held every little thing, remembered where it came from, and moved it two inches. Best afternoon I've had in months. No one needed anything from me, and the cookies came out perfect. That is not bored. That is a very full calendar with all my favorite people on it, which is me.
posts.first: A friend called on Sunday to see what I was up to. I said I was busy. She asked with what. I listed four things and she said, okay, you win. I did not feel like I was competing, but I will take the win.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a happy woman with pink curls standing in a cozy living room with a houseplant, stack of books, tray of cookies, record player and shelf of treasures, holding a glass of wine. Text at the top reads: Don’t you get bored being home all the time?” Meanwhile I bake, garden, read, rearrange my treasures, try new recipes, watch my shows, play music, sit outside, do little projects, and enjoy my own company. With zero nonsense.

posts.quote: My midlife goals are simple. Stay healthy-ish, keep the house tidy-ish, and stay emotionally stable-ish. It’s going okay-ish.
posts.caption: The laundry basket has been in the hallway since Tuesday. It has become a landmark. People give directions by it.
posts.first: My last checkup went fine. The doctor said healthy-ish was a very reasonable target for someone my age and I decided that was a compliment. I wrote it on the fridge next to the grocery list I forgot to take.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a woman with a messy bun shrugging in a kitchen with a half-tidy counter and a full laundry basket, holding a glass of wine. Text at the top reads: My midlife goals are simple. Stay healthy-ish, keep the house tidy-ish, and stay emotionally stable-ish. It’s going okay-ish.

posts.quote: I don’t trust people who don’t like animals. But I completely trust animals who don’t like people.
posts.caption: Mr. Whiskers has opinions about everyone. The mailman, my sister, the vacuum, the neighbor's visiting grandson. Me, he tolerates. I take that as the highest honor available. Tonight he climbed into my lap, turned around twice, and glared at the room like he was daring someone to say something. That's my guy.
posts.first: He came with the house, more or less. He walked in on day one, inspected the armchair, and claimed it. I got the other one. We've shared the living room ever since with no complaints, mostly his.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a calm woman with pink curls in a floral armchair with a grumpy scowling gray cat in her lap and a glass of wine on a side table. Text at the top reads: I don’t trust people who don’t like animals. But I completely trust animals who don’t like people.

posts.quote: Nobody warns you that a full night of sleep becomes something you brag about at brunch.
posts.first: Seven hours straight, last Tuesday. I told three people before lunch. One of them clapped. It was the best I've felt all fall, and I'd do it again tonight if my brain agrees.

posts.quote: The most confusing candy ever invented. Shaped like a peanut. Tastes like a banana. Feels like chewing a couch cushion.
posts.caption: Every October a bowl of these shows up at somebody's house and nobody admits to buying them. I took one. I was ready. I know what they taste like and I still checked. Banana. Peanut-shaped banana. Texture of a seat cushion. I ate three, for science, and I'd like it on the record that I'm not sure I enjoyed it.
posts.first: My mother-in-law keeps a bowl of them by the door all month. She loves them. I've watched trick-or-treaters pick one, look at it, and quietly put it back. I admire her commitment. I stand with the kids.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a puzzled woman at a table holding up an orange peanut-shaped candy with a squinting grimace, a jack-o'-lantern bowl of the candies in front of her and a glass of wine nearby. Text at the top reads: The most confusing candy ever invented. Shaped like a peanut. Tastes like a banana. Feels like chewing a couch cushion.

posts.quote: I ran to the store for milk and came home with cookies, a houseplant, and a nice long chat. The milk is still at the store.
posts.caption: The woman by the plants told me about her fern for eleven minutes. I learned a lot about fern light. I bought a fern.
posts.first: My husband asked where the milk was. I held up the plant like it was an answer. He said okay, and went to make toast. We eat our cereal dry on Thursdays now, apparently.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a pleased, slightly bewildered woman at her front door carrying a bag of cookies and a potted houseplant, with an empty hand where the milk should be. Text at the top reads: I ran to the store for milk and came home with cookies, a houseplant, and a nice long chat. The milk is still at the store.

posts.quote: At my age, a trail of clothes leading to the bedroom just means I dropped some on the way from the dryer.
posts.caption: A sock here, a towel there, one shirt that's been giving up since the kitchen. I picked up most of them eventually. The sock by the bedroom door I walked over twice, and at that point it felt like it was part of the house. The dryer buzzed at 6:40 and I carried the whole warm pile like a baby, and still lost a third of it before the hall ended.
posts.first: The only person who ever follows that trail is me, an hour later, picking it all up with a groan and a glass of wine in the other hand. It's honestly the most exercise I get all evening.
posts.alt: Cartoon illustration of a wry woman in a hallway holding an overflowing laundry basket and a glass of wine, with socks and shirts scattered along the floor behind her toward a bedroom door. Text at the top reads: At my age, a trail of clothes leading to the bedroom just means I dropped some on the way from the dryer.

stories.quote: Chocolate is God’s way of apologizing for Brussels sprouts.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a blissful woman at a kitchen table with a plate of Brussels sprouts pushed aside, holding a bar of chocolate. Text at the top reads: Chocolate is God’s way of apologizing for Brussels sprouts.

stories.quote: Don’t let someone else’s misery make you feel guilty about your own happiness.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a serene woman sitting on a sunny porch step with a glass of white wine as a small gray rain cloud drifts away. Text at the top reads: Don’t let someone else’s misery make you feel guilty about your own happiness.

stories.quote: I’d give anything to go back and sit next to the people I miss, just one more time.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a wistful woman with pink curls sitting in a floral armchair by a window at sunset, holding a framed family photo, with a cup of tea beside her. Text at the top reads: I’d give anything to go back and sit next to the people I miss, just one more time.

stories.quote: Picture yourself without wine. Now slap yourself, and never do that again.
stories.alt: Cartoon illustration of a wide-eyed woman holding her own cheek in a mock-scolding pose beside a kitchen table with a glass of red wine. Text at the top reads: Picture yourself without wine. Now slap yourself, and never do that again.
